nodes.name: Proof of the reference-policy stability lemma
nodes.statement: The proof almost follows that of \citet[Lemma 2]{huang2023queue}. We adapt their proof here for completeness. For each interval $W_j$ in \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability}, let $T_0$ be the first round in $W_j$. Then \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) \\ &=\sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \\ &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (Q_n^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\right )\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ). \end{align*} For the first term, we have the following for every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, according to \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability}: \begin{align*} \sum_{t\in W_j} \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\ge \epsilon_W \lvert W_j\rvert. \end{align*} Thus, the first summation enjoys the following lower bound: \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) \\ &\ge \left (\sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\right ) \epsilon_W \lvert W_j\rvert=\epsilon_W \lvert W_j\rvert \times \lVert \bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1\ge \epsilon_W \sum_{t\in W_j} \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1-\epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R) (\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2, \end{align*} where the last step uses the fact that $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1 - \lVert \bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1\le \lVert \bm Q(t)-\bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1$ and the queue length increment bound in \Cref{lem:queue length increment}. For the second summation, again utilizing the bound on $\lVert \bm Q(t)-\bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1$, we have \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (Q_n^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\right )\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\\ &\ge -\sum_{t\in W_j} \lVert \bm Q(t)-\bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1\times \max_{t\in W_j} \max_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \max_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left \lvert \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) \right \rvert \\ &\ge -N^2 (2NM+R) (\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2\times (2NM+R)=-N^2 (2NM+R)^2 (\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2. \end{align*} Therefore, recall the assumption that $\sum_{j\in [J]}(\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2\le C_W T$, summing over $j=1,2,\ldots,J$ gives \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \\ &\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\right ] \nonumber\\ &=-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring{a}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))\right ]-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ], \end{align*} thus giving our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Adapting Huang et al.: on each window, freeze queues at the window start, apply the piecewise stability margin, bound the drift error by queue increments, sum over windows.

nodes.name: Proof of the Lyapunov drift lemma
nodes.statement:
According to \Cref{eq:multi-hop stability dynamics}, for any round $t\in [T]$, server $n\in {\mathcal N}$, and commodity $k\in {\mathcal N}$, we  egin{align*} (Q_n^{(k)}(t+1))^2&\le \left [Q_n^{(k)}(t)-\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)ight ]_+^2+\left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)ight )^2+\ &\quad 2 \left [Q_n^{(k)}(t)-\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)ight ]_+\left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)ight )\ &\le (Q_n^{(k)}(t))^2 - 2 Q_n^{(k)}(t) \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)ight ) + \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)ight )^2 + \ &\quad \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)ight )^2+2 Q_n^{(k)}(t) \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)ight )\ &= (Q_n^{(k)}(t))^2 - 2 Q_n^{(k)}(t) \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)ight ) + \ &\quad \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)ight )^2 + \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)ight )^2. \end{align*} Therefore, by definition of the Lyapunov function $L_t$ and the Lyapunov drift $\Delta( m Q(t))$,  egin{align*} \Delta( m Q(t))&\le - \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\middle \vert  m Q(t)ight ] +

nodes.statement_short: Square the queue dynamics, bound the quadratic terms, sum over time; nonnegativity by telescoping.

nodes.name: Guarantee of PFOL Algorithm
nodes.statement: Consider the OLO problem in \Cref{def:OLO}. Suppose that $\mathcal X$ has diameter $D=\sup_{\bm x,\bm y\in \mathcal X}\lVert \bm x-\bm y\rVert_1$ and all $\lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty \le 1$. Then there exists an algorithm, such that for any comparator sequence $\mathring{\bm x}_1,\mathring{\bm x}_2,\ldots,\mathring{\bm x}_T\in \mathcal X$, \begin{equation*} \text{D-Regret}_T^{\text{OLO}}(\mathring{\bm x}_1,\mathring{\bm x}_2,\ldots,\mathring{\bm x}_T)=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{1+\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log \left (T \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2\right )\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: For losses bounded by 1, PFOL has dynamic regret $O(\sqrt{D(D+P_T)}\sqrt{1+\sum_t\|g_t\|_\infty^2}\log(\cdot))$.
assumptions: Consider the OLO problem in \Cref{def:OLO}.
Suppose that $\mathcal X$ has diameter $D=\sup_{\bm x,\bm y\in \mathcal X}\lVert \bm x-\bm y\rVert_1$ and all $\lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty \le 1$.
conclusions: Then there exists an algorithm, such that for any comparator sequence $\mathring{\bm x}_1,\mathring{\bm x}_2,\ldots,\mathring{\bm x}_T\in \mathcal X$, \begin{equation*} \text{D-Regret}_T^{\text{OLO}}(\mathring{\bm x}_1,\mathring{\bm x}_2,\ldots,\mathring{\bm x}_T)=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{1+\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log \left (T \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2\right )\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:OLO guarantee appendix

nodes.name: Extension of PFOL to dual norms
nodes.statement: Note that, although the original analysis by \citet{cutkosky2020parameter} uses $\ell_2$-norm for both comparators $\{\mathring{\bm x}_t\}_{t=1}^T$ and loss vectors $\{\bm g_t\}_{t=1}^T$, it is straightforward to extend to a pair of dual norms, which is $\ell_1$-norm for $\{\mathring{\bm x}_t\}_{t=1}^T$ and $\ell_\infty$-norm for $\{\bm g_t\}_{t=1}^T$ in our case.
nodes.statement_short: The PFOL guarantee, proved for the $\ell_2$ norm, extends to the $\ell_1$/$\ell_\infty$ dual pair.

nodes.name: Proof of the AdaPFOL guarantee
nodes.statement: As $G$ changes only if $G_t>2\max_{s<t} G_s$, it cannot change for more than $\lceil \log_2 (\max_t G_t)\rceil$ times. For a fixed $G$, suppose that it is used for rounds $t_1,t_1+1,\ldots,t_2$, then we must have $G_t\le G$, $\forall t\in [t_1,t_2]$ as otherwise a new instance of \texttt{PFOL} will be launched. Therefore, as $\lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty\le G_t\le G$, we have $\lVert G^{-1} \bm g_t\rVert_\infty\le 1$. This allows us to apply \Cref{lem:OLO guarantee} and yield \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \langle G^{-1} \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \lVert G^{-1} \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T\right ). \end{equation*} Multiplying $G$ on both sides, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \langle \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T\right ). \end{equation} As all $[t_1,t_2]$'s form a partition of $[T]$, summing up all \Cref{eq:doubling trick single phase} gives \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T G_t\right )\right ), \end{equation*} which utilizes the fact that at most $\operatorname{\mathcal O}(\lceil \log_2 (\max_t G_t)\rceil)$ distinct $[t_1,t_2]$'s can occur.
nodes.statement_short: Doubling argument: within each phase of fixed scale $G$ apply the PFOL guarantee to rescaled losses; at most $\log_2\max G_t$ phases.

nodes.name: Single-phase regret bound
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \langle \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T\right ).
nodes.label: eq:doubling trick single phase

nodes.name: Proof of deciding a(t) via AdaPFOL
nodes.statement: According to the definitions of $C_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)$ and $\mathring C_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)$ together with \Cref{lem:OLO unbounded guarantee}, \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t=1}^T \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} (C_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring{C}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t))\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right )\middle \vert \bm Q(t)\right ] \\ &=\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t)\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ) \left (a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right )\\ &\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\Bigg (\sqrt{1+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \lVert \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t) - \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t+1)\rVert_1}\\ &\qquad \sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \big (C_{n,m}(t)(Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t))\big )^2}\\ &\qquad \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\Bigg ). \end{align*} As $C_{n,m}(t)\in [0,M]$, we can upper bound the RHS of the above inequality by \begin{equation*} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \sqrt{2M^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)^2}\log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ), \end{equation*} where $P_T^a\triangleq \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \lVert \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t) - \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t+1)\rVert_1$ is the path length of $\mathring{\bm a}(t)$. Taking expectations gives our conclusion.
nodes.section: B.4 Deciding $\bm a(t)$ via \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace Algorithm (Proof of 3.5)
nodes.statement_short: Apply the AdaPFOL guarantee per link and bound loss norms by queue lengths.

nodes.name: Proof of the multi-hop network stability theorem
nodes.statement: We first defer some calculations into \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability tedious calc}, which basically combines \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability network stability}, \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability Lyapunov}, and \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making} together. \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability tedious calc} says \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ). \end{align*} In \Cref{lem:3/4 with log self-bounding}, we will prove a self-bounding inequality that says, if $y\le f + y^{3/4} g \log y$, then $y\le \left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )^4$. Therefore, we can apply \Cref{lem:3/4 with log self-bounding} to conclude that \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] &= \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (f(T) + g(T)^4 \log^4 \left (2(f(T)^{1/4} + g(T))^2\right )\right )\\ &=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ) \operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(1)\right )^4. \end{align*} Since \begin{align*} \left (\sqrt{1+P_T^a}\right )^4\le \left (\sqrt{T^{1/2 - \delta_a}}\right )^4 = \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T (T^{1-2\delta_a}), \end{align*} we know $\left (\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ) \operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(1)\right )^4=\operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(T^{1-2\delta_a})=o_T(T)$. The conclusion then follows.
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)
nodes.statement_short: Use the calculation lemma to get $y\le f+g y^{3/4}\log y$, solve it with the self-bounding lemma, and use the path-length bound.

nodes.name: Calculations when proving the network stability theorem
nodes.statement: Following all the assumptions in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability main theorem}, we have \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)
nodes.statement_short: Under the stability theorem's assumptions, total queue length satisfies a self-bounding inequality $y\le f(T)+g(T)y^{3/4}\log y$.
assumptions: Following all the assumptions in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability main theorem}
conclusions: we have \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:multi-hop stability tedious calc

nodes.name: Proof of the network stability calculations
nodes.statement: Recall the piecewise stability assumption in \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability} infers \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability network stability}: \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \\ &\le-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring{a}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))\right ]-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ]. \end{align*} From the non-negativity of Lyapunov drifts in \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability Lyapunov}, we know \begin{align*} 0&\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] + \nonumber \\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T. \end{align*} Furthermore, recall the guarantee of \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace algorithm in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making} that \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} (\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring{\mu}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t))\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right )\right ]\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right )\text{,} \end{align*} Therefore, we are able to get \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T\\ &\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right ) + \\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T. \end{align*} \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} states that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_t\rvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 = \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{3/2}\right )$. From \Cref{lem:queue length increment}, any single queue $Q_n^{(k)}(t)$ satisfies $\lvert Q_n^{(k)}(t+1)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\rvert \le (2NM + R)$. Hence, applying \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} to $\{Q_n^{(k)}(t) / (2NM+R)\}_{t\in [T]}$ to every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2 = (2NM+R)^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (\frac{Q_n^{(k)}(t)}{2NM+R}\right )^2 =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{2NM+R} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{1.5}\right ). \end{equation*} Further noticing that \begin{equation*} \max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\le \sum_{t=1}^T M \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \lVert \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_1\le M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1, \end{equation*} the above inequality becomes \begin{align*} \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{3/4} \log T \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )\right ]\right )+\\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ). \end{align*} Noticing that $x\mapsto x^{3/4} \log (M x)$ is concave when $x$ is large enough, Jensen inequality then gives \begin{equation*} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{3/4} \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ) \right ]\right )= \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]\right ). \end{equation*} Therefore, if we define the auxiliary functions $f(T)$ and $g(T)$ as \begin{align*} f(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ), \end{align*} we are able to conclude that \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{align*} as claimed.
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)
nodes.statement_short: Chain piecewise stability, drift nonnegativity and the AdaPFOL guarantee; bound $\sum\|Q\|_2^2$ by $(\sum\|Q\|_1)^{3/2}$ and apply Jensen.

nodes.name: Proof of the reference-policy stability lemma (utility task)
nodes.statement: The proof of this lemma is identical to that of \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability network stability}, except for replacing the environment-generated $\bm \lambda(t)$ with the $\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)$ generated by the reference policy. For more details, please refer to \Cref{sec:multi-hop stability network stability appendix}.
nodes.statement_short: Identical to the stability-task proof with $\lambda(t)$ replaced by $\mathring\lambda(t)$.

nodes.name: Lyapunov Drift-Plus-Penalty Analysis
nodes.statement: Under the queue dynamics of \Cref{eq:multi-hop stability dynamics}, \begin{align*} &\quad -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t))a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right ] \nonumber\\ &\quad -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ]+V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t(\bm \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right ] \nonumber\\ &\le \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2)T +V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t(\bm \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.section: C.2 Lyapunov Drift-Plus-Penalty Analysis (Proof of C.2)
nodes.statement_short: The drift lemma with the utility gap $V\sum(g_t(\lambda)-g_t(\mathring\lambda))$ added to both sides.
assumptions: Under the queue dynamics of \Cref{eq:multi-hop stability dynamics}
conclusions: \begin{align*} &\quad -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t))a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right ] \nonumber\\ &\quad -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ]+V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t(\bm \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right ] \nonumber\\ &\le \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2)T +V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t(\bm \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:multi-hop utility Lyapunov

nodes.name: Proof of the Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty lemma
nodes.statement: The proof follows from applying \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability Lyapunov} and adding \begin{equation*} V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t(\bm \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right ] \end{equation*} to both sides.
nodes.section: C.2 Lyapunov Drift-Plus-Penalty Analysis (Proof of C.2)
nodes.statement_short: Apply the drift lemma and add the utility-gap term to both sides.

nodes.name: Proof of the AdaBGD guarantee
nodes.statement: Similar to the proof by \citet[Theorem 1]{zhao2021bandit}, let $\widehat \ell_t(\bm x)=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\bm v\in \mathbb B}[\ell_t(\bm x+\delta \bm v)]$ (where $\mathbb B=\{\bm x\in \mathbb R^d\mid \lVert \bm x\rVert\le 1\}$ is the unit ball in $\mathbb R^d$) and $\bm v_t=(1-\alpha_t)\bm u_t\in (1-\alpha_t) \mathcal X$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm x_t)-\ell_t(\bm u_t))=\sum_{t=1}^T (\widehat \ell_t(\bm y_t)-\widehat \ell_t(\bm v_t))+\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm x_t) - \widehat \ell_t(\bm y_t)) + \sum_{t=1}^T (\widehat \ell_t(\bm v_t) - \ell_t(\bm u_t)). \end{equation*} According to the original proof, the expectation of the latter two terms are controlled by $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T 2L \delta_t]$ and $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T (L\delta_t + L \alpha_t R)]$, respectively. For the first term, according to \citet[Lemma 2.1]{flaxman2005online}, $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\bm s_t}[\frac d\delta \ell_t(\bm x_t) \bm s_t]=\nabla \widehat \ell_t(\bm x_t)$. Therefore, since $\lVert \frac d{\delta_t} \ell_t(\bm x_t) \bm s_t\rVert\le \frac d{\delta_t} C_t$, we get from \Cref{lem:SGD with adaptive LR} that \begin{equation*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\widehat \ell_t(\bm x_t)-\widehat \ell_t(\bm v_t))\right ]\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+\frac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\eta_t}{2} \frac{d^2}{\delta_t^2} C_t^2\right ], \end{equation*} where $\widehat P_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\lVert \bm v_t-\bm v_{t+1}\rVert$, the path length of $\{\bm v_t\}_{t\in [T]}$, satisfies $\widehat P_T\le P_T$. This gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Following Zhao et al., split regret via the smoothed loss; bound the smoothing terms and apply projected SGD to the one-point gradient estimates.

nodes.name: Guarantee of Projected SGD
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\mathcal X$ is bounded by $[r,R]$, the $t$-th loss function $\ell_t$ is bounded by $[-C_t,C_t]$ and is $L$-Lipschitz. Further suppose that a stochastic gradient $\bm g_t$ can be calculated in round $t$ such that $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\bm g_t\mid \bm x_1,\ell_1,\ldots,\bm x_t,\ell_t]=\nabla \ell_t(\bm x_t)$ and $\lVert \bm g_t\rVert_2\le C_t$. The the iteration \begin{equation*} \bm x_{t+1}=\text{Proj}_{\mathcal X}\left [\bm x_t-\eta_t \bm g_t\right ] \end{equation*} ensures the following dynamic regret guarantee for any fixed $\bm u_1,\bm u_2,\ldots,\bm u_T\in \mathcal X$: \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm x_t)-\ell_t(\bm u_t))\le \frac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+\frac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\eta_t}{2} C_t^2, \end{equation*} where $P_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\lVert \bm u_t-\bm u_{t+1}\rVert$ is the path length of $\{\bm u_t\}_{t=1}^T$.
nodes.statement_short: Projected SGD with decreasing step sizes and unbiased bounded gradients has dynamic regret $7R^2/(4\eta_T)+P_TR/\eta_T+\sum\eta_tC_t^2/2$.
assumptions: Suppose that $\mathcal X$ is bounded by $[r,R]$, the $t$-th loss function $\ell_t$ is bounded by $[-C_t,C_t]$ and is $L$-Lipschitz.

Further suppose that a stochastic gradient $\bm g_t$ can be calculated in round $t$ such that $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\bm g_t\mid \bm x_1,\ell_1,\ldots,\bm x_t,\ell_t]=\nabla \ell_t(\bm x_t)$ and $\lVert \bm g_t\rVert_2\le C_t$.
conclusions: The the iteration \begin{equation*} \bm x_{t+1}=\text{Proj}_{\mathcal X}\left [\bm x_t-\eta_t \bm g_t\right ] \end{equation*} ensures the following dynamic regret guarantee for any fixed $\bm u_1,\bm u_2,\ldots,\bm u_T\in \mathcal X$: \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm x_t)-\ell_t(\bm u_t))\le \frac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+\frac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\eta_t}{2} C_t^2, \end{equation*} where $P_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\lVert \bm u_t-\bm u_{t+1}\rVert$ is the path length of $\{\bm u_t\}_{t=1}^T$.

nodes.name: Proof of deciding lambda(t) via AdaBGD
nodes.statement: For loss function $\ell_t(\bm \lambda)=\langle \bm Q(t),\bm \lambda\rangle - Vg_t(\bm \lambda)$, it is bounded by $C_t\triangleq \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + V G$ and is $L_t\triangleq (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)$-Lipschitz. As $\bm Q(t)$ is revealed after the $(t-1)$-th round, $G_t$ and $L_t$ are both $\mathcal F_{t-1}$-measurable. As sketched in the main text, we first regard $\eta_t$ as a constant and tune $\delta_t$ to minimize the summation term in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee}. Let $\delta_t=(\eta_t d^2 C_t^2 / L_t)^{1/3}$ and $\alpha_t=\delta_t / r$. Suppose that all conditions in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee} hold, then \begin{align} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t)-\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t^\ast))\right ]\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{7R^2 + 4 P_T R}{4\eta_T} + \sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t \frac{d^2}{\delta_t^2} C_t^2 + 3L_t\delta_t + L_t \alpha_t R\right )\right ] \nonumber\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t d^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3} \frac{R}{r}\right ]\right ). \end{align} We first only keep the last term in \Cref{eq:true learning rate in BCO appendix}, \textit{i.e.}, let \begin{equation} \eta_t = \left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\middle / \sum_{s=1}^t \left ((\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4}, \end{equation} then we have $\eta_1>\eta_2>\cdots >\eta_T$. Let's first pretend the other condition of $\alpha_t<1$ from \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee} also holds at this moment. \Cref{lem:3/4 summation lemma} reveals that if $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, then $\left .\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \middle / (\sum_{s\le t} x_s)^{1/4} \right . =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4}\right )$. Plugging in $x_t=\left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}$, \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t)-\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t^\ast))\right ] \\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} R \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4} \right ]\right . + \\ &\qquad \left .\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R}{r} \left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\right )^{1/4} d^{2/3} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4} \right ] \right )\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\right ), \end{align*} where the last step utilizes $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty \le \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2$. This almost recovers our conclusion, so it only remains to ensure $\alpha_t=\delta_t/r<1$, which is equivalent to $\eta_t d^2 C_t^2 / L_t < r^3$, \textit{i.e.}, \begin{equation*} \eta_t^{-1} > r^{-3} d^2 \frac{(\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2}{\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL}. \end{equation*} Consider adding a term $X$ into the denominator of \Cref{eq:learning rate in BCO}. As $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty \le \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2$, $(\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 / (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)\le 2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty^2 / \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2) + 2 ((VG)^2 / (VL))\le 2 \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + 2 VG^2 / L$. So we only need to show \begin{align*} \frac{\left (X + \sum_{s=1}^t \left ((\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4}}{(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{3/4}} > 2 r^{-3} d^2 \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + V \frac{G^2}{L}\right ). \end{align*} We decompose $X$ into $X_1$ and $X_2$ and use them to cancel the two terms on the RHS, respectively. That is, we want \begin{align*} X_1 + \sum_{s=1}^t \left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty^2 \lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2^2\right )^{1/3} & > C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} \left (r^{-3} d^2 \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty\right )^{4/3},\\ X_2 + t^{3/4} (V^4 G^2 L^2)^{1/4} & > C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} \left (r^{-3} d^2 V G^2 / L\right )^{4/3}. \end{align*} We first craft $X_1$. In \Cref{lem:4/3 lower bound}, we show that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_t\rvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge (x_T/4)^{7/3}$. Thus, using the fact that $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty\le \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2$ and the queue length increment bound $\lvert \lVert \bm Q(t+1)\rVert_\infty - \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty \rvert\le (2NM+R)$ (\Cref{lem:queue length increment}), we can let $x_t=\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty / (2NM+R)$ and lower bound the LHS by \begin{equation*} X_1 + \sum_{s=1}^t \left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty^2 \lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2^2\right )^{1/3}\ge X_1+\frac{\left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty / 4 \right )^{7/3}}{(2NM+R)}\ge X_1^{3/7} \left (\frac{\left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty / 4 \right )^{7/3}}{(2NM+R)}\right )^{4/7}, \end{equation*} where the inequality results from AM-GM inequality $\frac{ax + by}{a+b} \ge \sqrt[a+b]{x^a y^b}$. Therefore, we only need to ensure $X_1^{3/7}\ge C^r T^{1/2-\delta_r} (4 r^{-3} d^2)^{4/3} (2NM+R)^{4/7}$. Setting $X_1$ as following then suffices. \begin{equation*} X_1=\left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\right )^{7/3} \left (4r^{-3} d^2 \right )^{28/9} \left ((2NM+R)\right )^{4/3}. \end{equation*} For $X_2$, we only need to set $X_2 = C^r T^{1/2-\delta_r} (r^{-3} d^2 VG^2 / L)^{4/3}$. Plugging back $X=X_1+X_2$, we get the learning rate scheduling defined in \Cref{eq:true learning rate in BCO appendix}. Now we verify that the two terms on the RHS of \Cref{eq:BCO regret decomposition} does not increase too much due to $X$. For the first term, \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{\eta_T}\right ]\\ &=\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{3/4}}\left (X + \sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R\right ) \left (\frac{X}{C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}}\right )^{3/4}+(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} R \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3} \right )^{3/4}\right ]\right )\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O} \left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^r T^{1/2-\delta_r})^2 + R (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{s=1}^t \left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3} \right )^{3/4}\right ]\right ). \end{align*} For the second term, as $\eta_t$ is strictly smaller than that in \Cref{eq:learning rate in BCO}, we can again apply \Cref{lem:3/4 summation lemma} (if $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, then $\left .\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \middle / (\sum_{s\le t} x_s)^{1/4} \right . =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4}\right )$) to conclude \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t d^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3} \frac{R}{r}\right ]\\ &=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3} (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]. \end{align*} Summing up two parts gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Tune $\delta_t$ given $\eta_t$, pick $\eta_t$ via the 3/4 summation lemma, and add terms $X_1,X_2$ to the denominator so that $\alpha_t<1$. The key step lower-bounds $\sum\|q_s\|^{4/3}$ to construct $X_1$.

nodes.name: BCO regret decomposition
nodes.statement: &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t)-\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t^\ast))\right ]\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{7R^2 + 4 P_T R}{4\eta_T} + \sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t \frac{d^2}{\delta_t^2} C_t^2 + 3L_t\delta_t + L_t \alpha_t R\right )\right ] \nonumber\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t d^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3} \frac{R}{r}\right ]\right ).
nodes.label: eq:BCO regret decomposition

nodes.name: Simplified learning rate for BCO
nodes.statement: \eta_t = \left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\middle / \sum_{s=1}^t \left ((\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4},

nodes.name: Proof of the multi-hop utility maximization theorem
nodes.statement:
As sketched in the main text, the first step is to 	extit{i)} combine algorithmic guarantees for 	exttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace (\Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making}) and 	exttt{AdaBGD}\xspace (\Cref{thm:multi-hop utility decision making}), 	extit{ii)} plug in the network stability assumption \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility network stability}, and 	extit{iii)} make use of the Lyapunov DPP analysis in \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility Lyapunov}. Deferring these calculations to \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility tedious calc}, we can get  egin{align} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]&\le - rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ] + f(T) + 
onumber \ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ] + 
onumber \ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{7/8}. \end{align} where  egin{align*} f(T)&= \epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T +  rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2ight .+\ &\qquad \qquad \left .\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+ rac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) Tight ),\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4} M \sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2 - \delta_a}} \log T ight ), \ h(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/8} \left ( rac Rr d^{2/3} + Right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4}ight ). \end{align*} \paragraph{Step 1 (Develop a Coarse Average Queue Length Bound).} Recall the assumption that $g_t$ is uniformly bounded by $[-G,G]$. Therefore, the first term on the RHS of \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding} is bounded by $2 rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT$ in absolute value. In \Cref{lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding}, we develop a self-bounding property that says, if $y\le f+y^{3/4} g \log y +y^{7/8}$, then $y=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (f+g^4 \log^8\left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2ight )+h^8ight )$. Therefore, applying it to \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding}, we have  egin{align} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]&\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (2 rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T) + g(T)^4 \log^8\left (2(f(T)^{1/8}+g(T)^{1/2}+h(T))^2ight ) + h(T)^8ight ) 
onumber\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight ) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (T^{1-2\delta_a} \log^8 \left (T^{1/4} + T^{1/4-\delta_a/2} + T^{1/4-\delta_\lambda/2}ight ) + T^{1-2\delta_\lambda}ight ) 
onumber\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight )+o_T(1). \end{align} As mentioned in the proof sketch of this theorem, this only gives a $ rac 1T\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(V)$ bound on the average queue length, which violates the system stability condition \Cref{eq:average queue}. However, this inequality can be used to derive the polynomial convergence result on the utility, which in turn refines the average queue length bound. \paragraph{Step 2 (Yield Polynomial Convergence on the Utility).} Moving the difference in the average utility in \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding} to the LHS, we have  egin{align*}  rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ]&\le -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ] + f(T) + 
onumber \ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ] + 
onumber \ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{7/8}. \end{align*} Plugging in the just-derived bound on average queue length, namely \Cref{eq:coarse queue length bound}, we have  egin{align*} &\quad  rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ]\ &\le 0 + f(T) + g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight )^{3/4} \log \left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight ) + h(T) \left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight )^{7/8}ight )\ &=f(T) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T \left (T^{1/4 - \delta_a/2} (VT)^{3/4} \log(VT) + T^{1/8 - \delta_\lambda / 4} (VT)^{7/8}ight ). \end{align*} According to the assumption that $V=o_T(\min\{T^{2\delta_a/3},T^{2\delta_\lambda/7}\})$, the second term on the RHS is of order $o_T(T)$. Therefore, we have  egin{align} &\quad  rac 1T \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)))ight )ight ]= rac{\epsilon_W}{VT} f(T) +  rac{\epsilon_W}{VT} o_T(T) 
onumber \ &=(VT)^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T +  rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2ight .+ 
onumber\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad \left .\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+ rac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) Tight )+o_T(V^{-1}) 
onumber\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{(N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W + (N^4 M^2+N^2 R^2)}{V}ight ) + o_T(V^{-1}). \end{align} The second conclusion of this theorem follows. \paragraph{Step 3 (Refine the Average Queue Length Bound).} Now we are ready to refine our average queue length bound using \Cref{eq:refined utility bound}. Instead of controlling the utility with the uniform boundedness assumption that $g_t\in [-G,G]$, we utilize the just-derived convergence result \Cref{eq:refined utility bound}. Specifically, again applying the self-bounding property in \Cref{lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding} to \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding} but instead replacing the first term on the RHS with \Cref{eq:refined utility bound}, we get  egin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]&\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (f(T) + o_T(T) + f(T) + g(T)^4 \log^8\left (2(f(T)^{1/8}+g(T)^{1/2}+h(T))^2ight ) + h(T)^8ight )\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}(f(T)) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (g(T)^4 \log^8\left (2(f(T)^{1/8}+g(T)^{1/2}+h(T))^2ight ) + h(T)^8ight ) + o_T(T) \ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{(N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W + (N^4 M^2+N^2 R^2)}{\epsilon_W} Tight ) + o_T(T), \end{align*} which gives our first conclusion as well.
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)
nodes.statement_short: Self-bounding inequality from the calculation lemma, then three steps: coarse queue bound, polynomial utility convergence, refined queue bound.

nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ] + f(T) + \nonumber \\ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] + \nonumber \\ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{7/8}.

nodes.statement: Under the conditions of \Cref{thm:multi-hop utility main theorem}, we have \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ] + f(T) + \\ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] + \\ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{7/8}. \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f(T)&= \epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T + \frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2\right .+\\ &\qquad \qquad \left .\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+\frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4} M \sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2 - \delta_a}} \log T \right ), \\ h(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/8} \left (\frac Rr d^{2/3} + R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4}\right ). \end{align*}

nodes.statement_short: Total queue length is bounded by the scaled utility gap plus $f(T)+g(T)y^{3/4}\log(My)+h(T)y^{7/8}$.
assumptions: Under the conditions of \Cref{thm:multi-hop utility main theorem}
conclusions: we have \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ] + f(T) + \\ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] + \\ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{7/8}. \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f(T)&= \epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T + \frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2\right .+\\ &\qquad \qquad \left .\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+\frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4} M \sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2 - \delta_a}} \log T \right ), \\ h(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/8} \left (\frac Rr d^{2/3} + R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4}\right ). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of the utility maximization calculations
nodes.statement:
From the network stability assumption, we derived in \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility network stability} that  egin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)ight ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T 
onumber\ &\le -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mathring \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))ight ] - \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \mathring \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)ight ]. \end{align*} Recall the 	exttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace guarantee in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making} that  egin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} (\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring{\mu}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t))\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)ight )ight ]\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert  m Q_m(t) -  m Q_n(t)Vert_\inftyight )ight ]ight )	ext{,} \end{align*} and the Bandit Convex Optimization guarantee in \Cref{thm:multi-hop utility decision making} that  egin{align*} &\scalemath{0.95}{\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\langle  m Q(t), m \lambda(t)angle - Vg_t( m \lambda(t))) - (\langle  m Q(t),\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)angle - Vg_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)))ight )ight ]}\ &\scalemath{0.95}{=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^2ight )+\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2 + V(L+G)ight )^{4/3}ight )^{3/4}ight ]ight ),} \end{align*} we therefore have  egin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)ight ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T 
onumber\ &\le -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))ight ] + \ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert  m Q_m(t) -  m Q_n(t)Vert_\inftyight )ight ]ight )+\ &\quad - \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)ight ] - V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t))-g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ]+\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^2ight )+\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2 + V(L+G)ight )^{4/3}ight )^{3/4}ight ]ight ). \end{align*} Further plugging in the Lyapunov DPP calculation in \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility Lyapunov} (which controls the three $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \cdots]$ terms outside $\operatorname{\mathcal O}$ on the RHS), we have  egin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)ight ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T 
onumber\ &\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert  m Q_m(t) -  m Q_n(t)Vert_\inftyight )ight ]ight )+\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^2ight )+\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2 + V(L+G)ight )^{4/3}ight )^{3/4}ight ]ight )+\ &\quad  rac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2)+V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t( m \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)))ight ]. \end{align*} For notational simplicity, we can abbreviate this inequality as  egin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]\le - rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ]+\widetilde f(T)+\ &\quad \widetilde g(T) \sqrt{\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^2ight ]} \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert  m Q_m(t)- m Q_n(t)Vert_\inftyight ) + \widetilde h(T) \left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^{4/3}ight ]ight )^{3/4}, \end{align*} where  egin{align*} \widetilde f(T)&= \epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T +  rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2ight .+\ &\qquad \qquad \left .\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+ rac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) Tight ),\ \widetilde g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M \sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2 - \delta_a}} \log T ight ), \ \widetilde h(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left ( rac Rr d^{2/3} + Right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4}ight ). \end{align*} To handle the $\widetilde g(T)$-related term, we use the argument same to that of \Cref{sec:multi-hop stability main theorem}: \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} states that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_tvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 = \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{3/2}ight )$. From \Cref{lem:queue length increment}, any single queue $Q_n^{(k)}(t)$ satisfies $\lvert Q_n^{(k)}(t+1)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)vert \le (2NM + R)$. Hence, applying \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} to $\{Q_n^{(k)}(t) / (2NM+R)\}_{t\in [T]}$ to every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, we have  egin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^2 = (2NM+R)^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left ( rac{Q_n^{(k)}(t)}{2NM+R}ight )^2 =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{2NM+R} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight )^{1.5}ight ). \end{equation*} Further noticing that  egin{equation*} \max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert  m Q_m(t) -  m Q_n(t)Vert_\infty\le \sum_{t=1}^T M \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \lVert  m Q_n(t)Vert_1\le M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1, \end{equation*} the $\widetilde g(T)$-related term then becomes  egin{align*} &\quad \widetilde g(T) \sqrt{\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^2ight ]} \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert  m Q_m(t)- m Q_n(t)Vert_\inftyight )\ &=\widetilde g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight )^{3/4} \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight )ight ]ight ). \end{align*} Noticing that $x\mapsto x^{3/4} \log (M x)$ is concave when $x$ is large enough, Jensen inequality then gives  egin{equation*} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight )^{3/4} \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ) ight ]ight )= \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]ight ). \end{equation*} Moreover, we handle the $\widetilde h(T)$-related term using \Cref{lem:4/3 upper bound}, a variant of \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} which states that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_tvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} = \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{7/6}ight )$. Hence, still applying it to $\{Q_n^{(k)}(t) / (2NM + R)\}_{t\in [T]}$ for every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$,  egin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_2^{4/3}&=\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)^2ight )^{2/3}\le \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)^{4/3}\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (2NM+Right )^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight )^{7/6}ight ). \end{align*} Therefore, we have  egin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]&\le - rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ] + \widetilde f(T) + \ &\quad \widetilde g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4}ight ) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ] + \ &\quad \widetilde h(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/8}ight ) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{7/8}. \end{align*} Setting $f(T)=\widetilde f(T)$, $g(T)=\widetilde g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}((2NM+R)^{1/4})$, and $h(T)=\widetilde h(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}((2NM+R)^{1/8})$ gives our conclusion.
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)
nodes.statement_short: Combine reference-policy stability, AdaPFOL and AdaBGD guarantees and the DPP inequality, then bound the $\ell_2$ and $\ell_{4/3}$ queue terms by powers of $\sum\|Q\|_1$.

nodes.name: Summation lemma
nodes.statement: The first lemma extends the famous summation lemma $\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{\sqrt{\sum_{s=1}^t x_s}}=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T x_t}\right )$ \citep{auer2002nonstochastic}.
conclusions: $\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{\sqrt{\sum_{s=1}^t x_s}}=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T x_t}\right )$

nodes.name: 3/4 summation lemma
nodes.statement: For non-negative real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T\in \mathbb R$, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{\left (\sum_{s=1}^t x_s\right )^{1/4}} \le 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: non-negative real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T\in \mathbb R$
nodes.statement_short: $\sum_t x_t/(\sum_{s\le t}x_s)^{1/4}\le 2(\sum_t x_t)^{3/4}$ for nonnegative $x_t$.
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{\left (\sum_{s=1}^t x_s\right )^{1/4}} \le 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:3/4 summation lemma

nodes.name: Proof of the 3/4 summation lemma
nodes.statement: Prove by induction. The case when $T=1$ is obvious. Suppose that the conclusion holds for $T-1$, then consider some $x_T$: \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{\left (\sum_{s=1}^t x_s\right )^{1/4}}\\ &= \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \frac{x_t}{\left (\sum_{s=1}^t x_s\right )^{1/4}} + \frac{x_T}{\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}}\\ &\le 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{3/4} + \frac{x_T}{\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}}, \end{align*} so it suffices to prove $\left . x_T \middle / \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}\right .\le 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4} - 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{3/4}$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4} - \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{3/4}\right )\left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}+\left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{1/4}\right )\\ &=\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \right ) + \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \right )^{3/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t \right )^{1/4} - \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \right )^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t \right )^{3/4} - \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t \right ) \\ &\ge x_T, \end{align*} where the last inequality uses $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\ge \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t$ (follows from $x_T\ge 0$). Hence, due to the fact that \begin{equation*} \left . x_T \middle / 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}\right .\le \left . x_T \middle / \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4} + \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{1/4}\right ., \end{equation*} the conclusion holds for $T$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $T$, reducing to an elementary inequality between successive partial sums.

nodes.name: 4/3-power lower bound
nodes.statement: Suppose that $x_1=0$, $x_2,x_3,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, and $\lvert x_t-x_{t-1}\rvert\le 1$, $\forall t=2,3,\ldots,T$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge 4^{-7/3} x_T^{7/3}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: $x_1=0$, $x_2,x_3,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, and $\lvert x_t-x_{t-1}\rvert\le 1$, $\forall t=2,3,\ldots,T$
nodes.statement_short: A nonnegative 1-Lipschitz sequence from 0 has $\sum x_t^{4/3}\ge 4^{-7/3}x_T^{7/3}$.
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge 4^{-7/3} x_T^{7/3}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:4/3 lower bound

nodes.name: Proof of the 4/3-power lower bound
nodes.statement: As adjacent $x_t$'s differ by no more than $1$, $\lfloor x_T\rfloor < T$ and $x_{T-t}\ge x_T - t$. Therefore, \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} x_{T-t}^{4/3}\ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} (x_T-t)^{4/3} \ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} \left (t^{4/3} + (x_T - \lfloor x_T\rfloor)^{4/3}\right )\ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} t^{4/3}, \end{equation*} where the last step uses $(a+b)^{4/3} \ge a^{4/3} + b^{4/3}$. As \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=0}^n i^{4/3} \ge \sum_{i=\lfloor \frac n2 \rfloor}^n i^{4/3} \ge \left (n - \left \lfloor \frac n2 \right \rfloor\right ) \left (\left \lfloor \frac n2 \right \rfloor\right )^{4/3} \ge \left (\left \lfloor \frac n2 \right \rfloor\right )^{7/3}, \end{equation*} we have $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge (\lfloor \frac{x_T}{2}\rfloor )^{7/3}$. If $x_T\ge 4$, then $\lfloor \frac{x_T}{2}\rfloor \ge \frac{x_T}{2}-1 \ge \frac{x_T}{4}$, giving the conclusion. Otherwise, \textit{i.e.}, $x_T<4$, then we naturally have $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge (\frac{x_T}{4})^{4/3}\ge (\frac{x_T}{4})^{7/3}$, so our conclusion still follows.
nodes.statement_short: The last $\lfloor x_T\rfloor$ terms are at least $x_T-t$; sum powers and split on $x_T\ge 4$.

nodes.name: Square-sum upper bound
nodes.statement: If $x_1=0$, $x_2,x_3,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, and $\lvert x_t-x_{t-1}\rvert\le 1$, $\forall t=2,3,\ldots,T$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 \le 4 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/2}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: $x_1=0$, $x_2,x_3,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, and $\lvert x_t-x_{t-1}\rvert\le 1$, $\forall t=2,3,\ldots,T$
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 \le 4 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/2}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:2 upper bound

nodes.name: 4/3-power upper bound
nodes.statement: If $x_1=0$, $x_2,x_3,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, and $\lvert x_t-x_{t-1}\rvert\le 1$, $\forall t=2,3,\ldots,T$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \le 2^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{7/6}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: $x_1=0$, $x_2,x_3,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, and $\lvert x_t-x_{t-1}\rvert\le 1$, $\forall t=2,3,\ldots,T$
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \le 2^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{7/6}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:4/3 upper bound

nodes.name: Proof of the 4/3-power upper bound
nodes.statement: Imitating the proof of \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} \citep[Lemma 4]{huang2023queue}, we short $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T$ as $y_1\le y_2\le \cdots \le y_T$. According to the original proof, $y_T=\max_{t\in [T]} x_t\le (2 \sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{1/2}$. Hence, \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \le y_T^{1/3} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t \le \left (2 \sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right ) = 2^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{7/6}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the maximum by $(2\sum x_t)^{1/2}$ as in Huang et al., then $\sum x_t^{4/3}\le \max^{1/3}\sum x_t$.

nodes.name: Self-bounding with 3/4 power and log
nodes.statement: If $y\le f + y^{3/4} g \log y$ and $f,g\ge 1$, then \begin{equation*} y^{1/4}\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ). \end{equation*}
assumptions: $y\le f + y^{3/4} g \log y$ and $f,g\ge 1$
conclusions: \begin{equation*} y^{1/4}\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:3/4 with log self-bounding

nodes.name: Proof of the 3/4-with-log self-bounding lemma
nodes.statement: Let $i(z) = z^4 - z^3 g \log (z^4) - f$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )^4\\ &\ge f + 4 \left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )^3 g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ). \end{align*} As $f,g\ge 1$, we have $2 (f^{1/4} + g)^2\ge f^{1/4} + g \log (2 (f^{1/4} + g)^2)$. Applying this relationship to the second log on the RHS of the inequality above, we yield \begin{equation*} i\left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )\ge 0. \end{equation*} On the other hand, from the conditions, we know $i(y^{1/4})\le 0$. Hence, if we can prove that $i(z)$ is monotone (at least for a range of $z$), we can conclude that $y^{1/4}\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )$, thus giving our conclusion. To conclude the monotonity of $i(z)$, we calculate its derivative as \begin{equation*} i'(z) = 4z^3 - 3z^2 g \log (z^4) - 4z^2 g. \end{equation*} Thus, if we only consider the case where $z\ge 0$, $i'(z)\ge 0$ holds when $z\ge 3g\log z + g$. Denoting the larger root of $z=3g\log z+g$ as $z_0$ (in case it has no root, let $z_0=1$), we know $i(z)$ is increasing in $[z_0,+\infty)$. Further observing that $f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )$ indeed satisfies $z\ge 3g\log z + g$, we know $f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\ge z_0$. On the other hand, from the assumption that $y\le f + y^{3/4} g \log y$, we know $i(y^{1/4})\le 0\le i(f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ))$. Our conclusion follows from discussing the relationship between $y^{1/4}$ and $z_0$: If $y^{1/4}\le z_0$, then we immediately have \begin{equation*} y^{1/4}\le z_0\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ). \end{equation*} Otherwise, according to the monotonity of $i(z)$ when $z\ge z_0$, we still have \begin{equation*} y^{1/4}\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ), \end{equation*} as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Study $i(z)=z^4-z^3g\log z^4-f$: it is nonnegative at the claimed bound and increasing beyond its largest critical root; compare $y^{1/4}$ with that root.

nodes.name: Self-bounding with 3/4 and 7/8 powers
nodes.statement: If $y \le f + y^{3/4} g \log y + y^{7/8} h$ and $f,g,h\ge 1$, then \begin{equation*} y^{1/8}\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h. \end{equation*}
assumptions: $y \le f + y^{3/4} g \log y + y^{7/8} h$ and $f,g,h\ge 1$
conclusions: \begin{equation*} y^{1/8}\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding

nodes.name: Proof of the 3/4-and-7/8 self-bounding lemma
nodes.statement: Let $i(z) = z^8 - f - z^6 g \log (z^8) - z^7 h$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^8 \\ &=\left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right )\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 h\\ &\ge \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^6 f^{1/4} + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^6 g \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 h \\ &\ge f + \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^6 g \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 h. \end{align*} As $f,g,h\ge 1$, we have $2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\ge f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h$. Applying it to the $(\cdots)^6 g \log(2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2)$ term on the RHS, we have \begin{equation*} i\left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right )+h\right )\ge 0 \end{equation*} On the other hand, from the conditions we know $i(y^{1/8})\le 0$. Hence, we again want to prove the monotony of $i(z)$, which gives the conclusion that $y^{1/8}\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} + h$. Calculating the derivative of $i(z)$, we have \begin{equation*} i'(z) = 8z^7 - 6z^5 g \log(z^8) - 8 z^5 g - 7z^6 h. \end{equation*} Thus, if we only consider the case where $z\ge 1$, $i'(z)\ge 0$ holds when $8z^2 - 6 g \log(z^8) - 8 g - 7z h\ge 0$. As $z^2$ is convex and $6g\log (z^8) + 8g + 7zh$ is concave, there are at most two intersections. Hence, again denoting the larger root of $8z^2 - 6 g \log(z^8) - 8 g - 7z h = 0$ as $z_0$ (in case there is no root, let $z_0=1$), $i(z)$ is monotonic in $[z_0,+\infty)$. As $f,g,h\ge 1$, $f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h \ge z_0$ always holds. The conclusion follows by discussing the relationship of $y^{1/8}$ and $z_0$: If $y^{1/8}\le z_0$, we directly have \begin{equation*} y^{1/8}\le z_0\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h. \end{equation*} Otherwise, we can still conclude \begin{equation*} y^{1/8}\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h \end{equation*} from the monotonity of $i(z)$ when $z\ge z_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Same monotonicity argument for $i(z)=z^8-f-z^6g\log z^8-z^7h$.

nodes.name: Compare the reference-policy bound with the drift bound
nodes.statement: The first step of the proof is comparing the guarantee from \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability} and that from Lyapunov drift analysis. Specifically, recall that \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability network stability} upper bounds the total queue length using $-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \langle \bm C_{n,m}(t) (\bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)),\mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t)\rangle]$ (together with some other terms, which are constants after taking expectations) while \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability Lyapunov} reveals the non-positivity of $-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \langle \bm C_{n,m}(t) (\bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)),{\bm a}_{n,m}(t)\rangle]$ (again, many constants omitted).
nodes.statement_short: Compare the reference-policy bound with the drift bound
nodes.section: 3.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability

nodes.name: Apply the AdaPFOL theorem to close the gap
nodes.statement: Furthermore, via the guarantee of \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace (\Cref{alg:OLO unbounded}) in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making}, these two terms are actually pretty close -- they only differ by $\operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T\left (\sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2-\delta_a}} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2}\right ]\right )$, where we used the assumption that $P_T^a\le C^a T^{1/2-\delta_a}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the AdaPFOL theorem to close the gap
nodes.section: 3.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability

nodes.name: Bound the l2 queue term by the 3/4 power of the l1 sum
nodes.statement: By a property that ensures $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 \le 4(\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{1/5}$ when $\lvert x_t-x_{t+1}\rvert\le 1$ (\Cref{lem:2 upper bound}), this $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2}\right ]$ can be controlled by $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the l2 queue term by the 3/4 power of the l1 sum
nodes.section: 3.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability

nodes.name: Assemble the self-bounding inequality
nodes.statement: Finishing these steps, which are detailed in \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability tedious calc}, we are able to conclude \begin{equation*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{equation*} where $f(T) = \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T)$ and $g(T) = \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T^{1/4-\delta_a/2})$ are some abstract functions to simplify notations.
nodes.statement_short: Assemble the self-bounding inequality
nodes.section: 3.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability

nodes.name: Recognize the self-bounding form
nodes.statement: Therefore, this inequality is in a self-bounding form that $y\le f+y^{3/4} g \log y$ where $y$ is the total queue lengths in $T$ rounds. As we informally stated in \Cref{eq:self-bounding informal}, this gives our system stability guarantee.
nodes.statement_short: Recognize the self-bounding form
nodes.section: 3.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability

nodes.name: Solve the self-bounding inequality
nodes.statement: Indeed, in \Cref{lem:3/4 with log self-bounding}, we show that $y\le f+y^{3/4} g \log y$ implies $y=\operatorname{\mathcal O}(f)+\operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}(g^4)$. Therefore, $y=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T)+\operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(T^{1-2\delta_a})$ and thus $\frac 1T \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the self-bounding inequality; conclude stability
nodes.section: 3.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability

nodes.name: Name the loss bound $C_t$ and Lipschitz constant $L_t$
nodes.statement: The terms $(\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty+VG)$ and $(\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2+VL)$ are the boundedness and Lipschitzness of $\ell_t$, respectively, which we denote by $C_t$ and $L_t$ to simplify notations.
nodes.statement_short: Name the loss bound $C_t$ and Lipschitz constant $L_t$

nodes.name: Tune $\delta_t$ to get the informal regret decomposition
nodes.statement: First suppose that all conditions in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee} are satisfied by our $\{\eta_t\}_{t\in [T]}$. To balance the term inside $\sum_{t=1}^T (\cdot)$ in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee} by fixing $\eta_t$ and altering $\delta_t$, one shall pick $\delta_t=(\eta_t d^2 C_t^2 / L_t)^{1/3}$ and roughly have (hiding many constant terms; see \Cref{eq:BCO regret decomposition} in the appendix for an accurate form): \begin{equation} \text{D-Regret}_T^{\text{BCO}}(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(1),\mathring{\bm \lambda}(2),\ldots,\mathring{\bm \lambda}(T))\lesssim \frac{C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda}}{\eta_T} + \sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t C_t^2 L_t^2\right )^{1/3}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Tune $\delta_t$ to get the informal regret decomposition

nodes.name: Choose $\eta_t$ via the 3/4 summation lemma
nodes.statement: We derive in \Cref{lem:3/4 summation lemma} that $\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{(\sum_{s\le t} x_s)^{1/4}}\lesssim (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{3/4}$, which is a variant of the famous summation lemma \citep{auer2002nonstochastic}. Therefore, if we pick $\eta_t\approx \left (\frac{C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda}}{\sum_{s=1}^t (C_t^2 L_t^2)^{1/3}}\right )^{3/4}$ (\textit{i.e.}, only keeping the third term in the denominator of \Cref{eq:true learning rate in BCO restatement}), \Cref{eq:BCO regret decomposition informal} becomes $\operatorname{\mathcal O}((C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[(\sum_{t=1}^T (C_t^2 L_t^2)^{1/3})^{3/4}])$. When focusing on $T$-related terms, this is roughly $\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T^{1/8-\delta_\lambda/4} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[(\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1)]^{7/8})$, which allows the self-bounding analysis similar to \Cref{eq:self-bounding informal}.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\eta_t$ via the 3/4 summation lemma

nodes.name: Extra denominator terms ensure $\alpha_t<1$
nodes.statement: However, such a configuration of $\{\eta_t\}_{t\in [T]}$ may not ensure the $\alpha_t = \delta_t / r = (\eta_t d^2 C_t^2 / L_t)^{1/3}/r<1$ condition in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee}. The other two terms in \Cref{eq:true learning rate in BCO restatement} are added for this purpose. We refer the readers to \Cref{sec:general bandit part appendix} for detailed verification.
nodes.statement_short: Extra denominator terms ensure $\alpha_t<1$

nodes.name: Obtain the self-bounding inequality from the calculation lem
nodes.statement: The first step of the proof is plugging the algorithmic guarantees for \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace (\Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making}) and for \texttt{AdaBGD}\xspace (\Cref{thm:multi-hop utility decision making}) into the reference policy assumption (\Cref{eq:multi-hop utility network stability}) and then making use of the Lyapunov DPP guarantee (\Cref{eq:multi-hop utility Lyapunov}). We present the detailed derivation in \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility tedious calc}. The conclusion reads \begin{align} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ] + f(T) + \nonumber\\ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] + h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{7/8}, \end{align} where $f(T)=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T)$, $g(T)=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T^{1/4-\delta_a/2})$, and $h(T)=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T^{1/8-\delta_\lambda/4})$.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the self-bounding inequality from the calculation lemma
nodes.section: 4.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization

nodes.name: Step 1: coarse $O_T(VT)$ queue bound
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 1 (Develop a Coarse Average Queue Length Bound).} By the boundedness of $g_t$, the first term on the RHS of \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding informal} is controlled by $\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} T G=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(VT)$ (note that, as $V=\text{poly}(T)$, $V$ is not a constant that can be hidden in $\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T$ and this term is actually super-linear).
