Similar to the one used when proving \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability main theorem}, we develop another self-bounding property that says $y\le f+y^{3/4}g\log y +y^{7/8}h$ infers $y=\operatorname{\mathcal O}(f)+\operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}(g^{4}) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}(h^8)$ (see \Cref{lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding}). Therefore, \begin{equation*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (VT + T\right ) + \operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T\left (T^{1-2\delta_a}\right ) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (T^{1 - 2 \delta_\lambda}\right )=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(VT), \end{equation*} only giving a $\frac 1T\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(V)=\omega_T(1)$ bound on the average queue length (violating the system stability condition \Cref{eq:average queue}). However, this inequality can be used to derive the polynomial convergence result on the utility, which in turn further refines the queue length bound.
nodes.statement_short: Step 1: coarse $O_T(VT)$ queue bound
nodes.section: 4.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization

nodes.name: Step 2: utility gap $O_T(1/V)$
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 2 (Yield Polynomial Convergence on the Utility).} Moving the difference in the average utility to the LHS in \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding informal} and plugging in the just-derived bound on average queue length, we have \begin{align*} \frac{V}{\epsilon_W T} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t)))\right )\right ]&=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (-0+\frac{f(T)}{T}+\frac{g(T)}{T}(VT)^{3/4}+\frac{h(T)}{T}(VT)^{7/8}\right )\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (1+\left (\frac{T^{1-2\delta_a}V^3}{T}\right )^{1/4}+\left (\frac{T^{1-2\delta_\lambda}V^7}{T}\right )^{1/8}\right ). \end{align*} According to the assumption that $V=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(\min\{T^{2\delta_a/3},T^{2\delta_\lambda/7}\})$, the RHS is of order $\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(1)$. Thus \begin{equation*} \frac 1T \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t)))\right )\right ]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(V^{-1}), \end{equation*} \textit{i.e.}, a polynomial convergence rate on the expected average utility is derived.
nodes.statement_short: Step 2: utility gap $O_T(1/V)$
nodes.section: 4.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization

nodes.name: Step 3: refined $O_T(T)$ queue bound
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 3 (Refine the Average Queue Length Bound).} Now we are ready to refine our average queue length bound. Instead of controlling the utility with boundedness $g_t\in [-G,G]$, we utilize the just-derived convergence result and yields (again using the self-bounding property in \Cref{lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding}) \begin{equation*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (V \times V^{-1} T + T\right ) + \operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T\left (T^{1-2\delta_a}\right ) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (T^{1-2\delta_\lambda}\right )=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(T), \end{equation*} that is, the average queue length $\frac 1T\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(1)$, which means \Cref{eq:average queue} holds and the system is stable. Putting Step 2 and Step 3 together gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Step 3: refined $O_T(T)$ queue bound; conclude
nodes.section: 4.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization

nodes.name: Pointer to the full proof
nodes.statement: Once again, we omitted all factors except for those $\text{poly}(T)$ ones throughout this proof sketch. Please refer to \Cref{sec:multi-hop utility appendix} for the complete version.
nodes.statement_short: Pointer to the full proof
nodes.section: 4.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization

nodes.name: Adapt the proof of Huang et al.
nodes.statement: The proof almost follows that of \citet[Lemma 2]{huang2023queue}. We adapt their proof here for completeness.
nodes.statement_short: Adapt the proof of Huang et al.

nodes.name: Fix the window start $T_0$ and split the sum
nodes.statement: For each interval $W_j$ in \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability}, let $T_0$ be the first round in $W_j$. Then \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) \\ &=\sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \\ &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (Q_n^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\right )\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fix the window start $T_0$ and split the sum

nodes.name: Apply the piecewise stability margin
nodes.statement: For the first term, we have the following for every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, according to \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability}: \begin{align*} \sum_{t\in W_j} \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\ge \epsilon_W \lvert W_j\rvert. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the piecewise stability margin

nodes.name: Lower-bound the first sum
nodes.statement: Thus, the first summation enjoys the following lower bound: \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) \\ &\ge \left (\sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\right ) \epsilon_W \lvert W_j\rvert=\epsilon_W \lvert W_j\rvert \times \lVert \bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1\ge \epsilon_W \sum_{t\in W_j} \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1-\epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R) (\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2, \end{align*} where the last step uses the fact that $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1 - \lVert \bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1\le \lVert \bm Q(t)-\bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1$ and the queue length increment bound in \Cref{lem:queue length increment}.
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the first sum

nodes.name: Lower-bound the second sum by queue increments
nodes.statement: For the second summation, again utilizing the bound on $\lVert \bm Q(t)-\bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1$, we have \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t\in W_j} \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (Q_n^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(T_0)\right )\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\\ &\ge -\sum_{t\in W_j} \lVert \bm Q(t)-\bm Q(T_0)\rVert_1\times \max_{t\in W_j} \max_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \max_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left \lvert \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) \right \rvert \\ &\ge -N^2 (2NM+R) (\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2\times (2NM+R)=-N^2 (2NM+R)^2 (\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the second sum by queue increments

nodes.name: Sum over windows and conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, recall the assumption that $\sum_{j\in [J]}(\lvert W_j\rvert-1)^2\le C_W T$, summing over $j=1,2,\ldots,J$ gives \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \\ &\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_n^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} C_{o,n}(t) \mathring a_{o,n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\right ] \nonumber\\ &=-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring{a}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))\right ]-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ], \end{align*} thus giving our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over windows and conclude

nodes.name: Expand the squared queue update
nodes.statement: According to \Cref{eq:multi-hop stability dynamics}, for any round $t\in [T]$, server $n\in {\mathcal N}$, and commodity $k\in {\mathcal N}$, we \begin{align*} (Q_n^{(k)}(t+1))^2&\le \left [Q_n^{(k)}(t)-\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right ]_+^2+\left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2+\\ &\quad 2 \left [Q_n^{(k)}(t)-\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right ]_+\left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\\ &\le (Q_n^{(k)}(t))^2 - 2 Q_n^{(k)}(t) \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2 + \\ &\quad \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2+2 Q_n^{(k)}(t) \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right )\\ &= (Q_n^{(k)}(t))^2 - 2 Q_n^{(k)}(t) \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2 + \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the squared queue update

nodes.name: Bound the drift
nodes.statement: Therefore, by definition of the Lyapunov function $L_t$ and the Lyapunov drift $\Delta(\bm Q(t))$, \begin{align*} \Delta(\bm Q(t))&\le - \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) - \sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) - \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\middle \vert \bm Q(t)\right ] + \nonumber\\ &\quad \frac 12 \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2 + \left (\sum_{(o,n)\in {\mathcal L}} \mu_{o,n}^{(k)}(t) + \lambda_{n}^{(k)}(t)\right )^2\middle \vert \bm Q(t)\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the drift

nodes.name: Bound the quadratic terms by constants
nodes.statement: Exchanging summations and using the bounded assumptions that $\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\in [0,M]$ and $\lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\in [0,R]$, we get \begin{align*} \Delta(\bm Q(t))&\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\middle \vert \bm Q(t)\right ] + \nonumber \\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the quadratic terms by constants

nodes.name: Take expectations and sum over $t$
nodes.statement: Taking expectation \textit{w.r.t.} $\bm Q(t)$ and summing up from $t=1,2,\ldots,T$, we have \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \Delta(\bm Q(t))\right ]&\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] + \nonumber \\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Take expectations and sum over $t$

nodes.name: Telescoping gives nonnegativity
nodes.statement: By telescoping sums, we know \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \Delta(\bm q_t)=L_{T+1}-L_1=L_{T+1}\ge 0, \end{equation*} where the last step uses the fact that $L_{T+1}$ is the sum of squares. Therefore, our conclusion follows.
nodes.statement_short: Telescoping gives nonnegativity; conclude

nodes.name: Few scale changes
nodes.statement: As $G$ changes only if $G_t>2\max_{s<t} G_s$, it cannot change for more than $\lceil \log_2 (\max_t G_t)\rceil$ times.
nodes.statement_short: Few scale changes

nodes.name: Consider one phase with fixed $G$
nodes.statement: For a fixed $G$, suppose that it is used for rounds $t_1,t_1+1,\ldots,t_2$, then we must have $G_t\le G$, $\forall t\in [t_1,t_2]$ as otherwise a new instance of \texttt{PFOL} will be launched.
nodes.statement_short: Consider one phase with fixed $G$

nodes.name: Apply the PFOL guarantee to rescaled losses
nodes.statement: Therefore, as $\lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty\le G_t\le G$, we have $\lVert G^{-1} \bm g_t\rVert_\infty\le 1$. This allows us to apply \Cref{lem:OLO guarantee} and yield \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \langle G^{-1} \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \lVert G^{-1} \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the PFOL guarantee to rescaled losses

nodes.name: Rescale the phase bound
nodes.statement: Multiplying $G$ on both sides, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \langle \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=t_1}^{t_2} \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T\right ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rescale the phase bound

nodes.name: Sum over phases
nodes.statement: As all $[t_1,t_2]$'s form a partition of $[T]$, summing up all \Cref{eq:doubling trick single phase} gives \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \langle \bm g_t,\bm x_t-\bm x_t^\circ\rangle=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{D \left (D+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \lVert \mathring{\bm x}_t-\mathring{\bm x}_{t+1}\rVert_1\right )}\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm g_t\rVert_\infty^2}\log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T G_t\right )\right ), \end{equation*} which utilizes the fact that at most $\operatorname{\mathcal O}(\lceil \log_2 (\max_t G_t)\rceil)$ distinct $[t_1,t_2]$'s can occur.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over phases; conclude

nodes.name: Apply the AdaPFOL guarantee per link
nodes.statement: According to the definitions of $C_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)$ and $\mathring C_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)$ together with \Cref{lem:OLO unbounded guarantee}, \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t=1}^T \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} (C_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring{C}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t))\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right )\middle \vert \bm Q(t)\right ] \\ &=\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t)\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ) \left (a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring a_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\right )\\ &\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\Bigg (\sqrt{1+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \lVert \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t) - \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t+1)\rVert_1}\\ &\qquad \sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \big (C_{n,m}(t)(Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t))\big )^2}\\ &\qquad \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\Bigg ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the AdaPFOL guarantee per link
nodes.section: B.4 Deciding $\bm a(t)$ via \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace Algorithm (Proof of 3.5)

nodes.name: Bound loss norms by queue lengths
nodes.statement: As $C_{n,m}(t)\in [0,M]$, we can upper bound the RHS of the above inequality by \begin{equation*} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \sqrt{2M^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)^2}\log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ), \end{equation*} where $P_T^a\triangleq \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \lVert \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t) - \mathring{\bm a}_{n,m}(t+1)\rVert_1$ is the path length of $\mathring{\bm a}(t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound loss norms by queue lengths
nodes.section: B.4 Deciding $\bm a(t)$ via \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace Algorithm (Proof of 3.5)

nodes.name: Take expectations
nodes.statement: Taking expectations gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Take expectations
nodes.section: B.4 Deciding $\bm a(t)$ via \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace Algorithm (Proof of 3.5)

nodes.name: Invoke the calculation lemma
nodes.statement: We first defer some calculations into \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability tedious calc}, which basically combines \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability network stability}, \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability Lyapunov}, and \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making} together. \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability tedious calc} says \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Invoke the calculation lemma
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Solve via the self-bounding lemma
nodes.statement: In \Cref{lem:3/4 with log self-bounding}, we will prove a self-bounding inequality that says, if $y\le f + y^{3/4} g \log y$, then $y\le \left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )^4$. Therefore, we can apply \Cref{lem:3/4 with log self-bounding} to conclude that \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] &= \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (f(T) + g(T)^4 \log^4 \left (2(f(T)^{1/4} + g(T))^2\right )\right )\\ &=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ) \operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(1)\right )^4. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Solve via the self-bounding lemma
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Path-length bound makes the $g^4$ term $o_T(T)$
nodes.statement: Since \begin{align*} \left (\sqrt{1+P_T^a}\right )^4\le \left (\sqrt{T^{1/2 - \delta_a}}\right )^4 = \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T (T^{1-2\delta_a}), \end{align*} we know $\left (\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ) \operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(1)\right )^4=\operatorname{\widetilde{\mathcal O}}_T(T^{1-2\delta_a})=o_T(T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Path-length bound makes the $g^4$ term $o_T(T)$
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The conclusion then follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Recall the reference-policy lemma
nodes.statement: Recall the piecewise stability assumption in \Cref{def:multi-hop stability network stability} infers \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability network stability}: \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \\ &\le-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} C_{n,m}(t) \mathring{a}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))\right ]-\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the reference-policy lemma
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Use drift nonnegativity
nodes.statement: From the non-negativity of Lyapunov drifts in \Cref{lem:multi-hop stability Lyapunov}, we know \begin{align*} 0&\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ) + \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] + \nonumber \\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use drift nonnegativity
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Recall the AdaPFOL theorem
nodes.statement: Furthermore, recall the guarantee of \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace algorithm in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making} that \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} (\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring{\mu}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t))\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right )\right ]\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right )\text{,} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the AdaPFOL theorem
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Combine the three bounds
nodes.statement: Therefore, we are able to get \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T\\ &\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right ) + \\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the three bounds
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Bound squared queue sums by the 3/2 power
nodes.statement: \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} states that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_t\rvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 = \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{3/2}\right )$. From \Cref{lem:queue length increment}, any single queue $Q_n^{(k)}(t)$ satisfies $\lvert Q_n^{(k)}(t+1)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\rvert \le (2NM + R)$. Hence, applying \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} to $\{Q_n^{(k)}(t) / (2NM+R)\}_{t\in [T]}$ to every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2 = (2NM+R)^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (\frac{Q_n^{(k)}(t)}{2NM+R}\right )^2 =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{2NM+R} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{1.5}\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound squared queue sums by the 3/2 power
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Bound the log term
nodes.statement: Further noticing that \begin{equation*} \max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\le \sum_{t=1}^T M \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \lVert \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_1\le M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1, \end{equation*} the above inequality becomes \begin{align*} \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{3/4} \log T \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )\right ]\right )+\\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the log term
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Apply Jensen's inequality
nodes.statement: Noticing that $x\mapsto x^{3/4} \log (M x)$ is concave when $x$ is large enough, Jensen inequality then gives \begin{equation*} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{3/4} \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ) \right ]\right )= \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Jensen's inequality
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Define $f,g$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, if we define the auxiliary functions $f(T)$ and $g(T)$ as \begin{align*} f(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1}\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2(2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R))C_W T + (N^4 M^2 + N^2 R^2)T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M (2NM+R)^{1/4} \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \log T\right ), \end{align*} we are able to conclude that \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le f(T) + g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ], \end{align*} as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Define $f,g$ and conclude
nodes.section: B.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Network Stability (Proof of 3.6)

nodes.name: Introduce the smoothed loss and decompose regret
nodes.statement: Similar to the proof by \citet[Theorem 1]{zhao2021bandit}, let $\widehat \ell_t(\bm x)=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\bm v\in \mathbb B}[\ell_t(\bm x+\delta \bm v)]$ (where $\mathbb B=\{\bm x\in \mathbb R^d\mid \lVert \bm x\rVert\le 1\}$ is the unit ball in $\mathbb R^d$) and $\bm v_t=(1-\alpha_t)\bm u_t\in (1-\alpha_t) \mathcal X$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm x_t)-\ell_t(\bm u_t))=\sum_{t=1}^T (\widehat \ell_t(\bm y_t)-\widehat \ell_t(\bm v_t))+\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm x_t) - \widehat \ell_t(\bm y_t)) + \sum_{t=1}^T (\widehat \ell_t(\bm v_t) - \ell_t(\bm u_t)). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the smoothed loss and decompose regret

nodes.name: Bound the smoothing terms
nodes.statement: According to the original proof, the expectation of the latter two terms are controlled by $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T 2L \delta_t]$ and $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T (L\delta_t + L \alpha_t R)]$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the smoothing terms

nodes.name: One-point gradient estimate is unbiased
nodes.statement: For the first term, according to \citet[Lemma 2.1]{flaxman2005online}, $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\bm s_t}[\frac d\delta \ell_t(\bm x_t) \bm s_t]=\nabla \widehat \ell_t(\bm x_t)$.
nodes.statement_short: One-point gradient estimate is unbiased

nodes.name: Apply projected SGD
nodes.statement: Therefore, since $\lVert \frac d{\delta_t} \ell_t(\bm x_t) \bm s_t\rVert\le \frac d{\delta_t} C_t$, we get from \Cref{lem:SGD with adaptive LR} that \begin{equation*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\widehat \ell_t(\bm x_t)-\widehat \ell_t(\bm v_t))\right ]\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+\frac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\eta_t}{2} \frac{d^2}{\delta_t^2} C_t^2\right ], \end{equation*} where $\widehat P_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\lVert \bm v_t-\bm v_{t+1}\rVert$, the path length of $\{\bm v_t\}_{t\in [T]}$, satisfies $\widehat P_T\le P_T$. This gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Apply projected SGD; conclude

nodes.name: Start with full feedback
nodes.statement: We first consider the full-feedback model where the whole $\ell_t$, instead of the single-entry $\ell_t(\bm x_t)$, is available.
nodes.statement_short: Start with full feedback

nodes.name: Dynamic regret of projected gradient descent
nodes.statement:
Then the Gradient Descent algorithm $ m x_{t+1}=	ext{Proj}_{\mathcal X}[ m x_t-\eta_t 
abla \ell_t( m x_t)]$ enjoys the following dynamic regret guarantee (which follows the proof of \citet[Theorem 2]{zinkevich2003online}):  egin{align} &\quad 	ext{D-Regret}_T( m u_1, m u_1,\ldots, m u_T)=\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t( m x_t)-\ell_t( m u_t)) 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{t=1}^T \left ( rac{1}{2\eta_t} \left (\lVert  m x_t- m u_tVert^2-\lVert  m x_{t+1}- m u_tVert^2ight )+ rac{\eta_t}{2}\lVert 
abla \ell_t( m x_t)Vert^2ight ) 
onumber\ &= \sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\lVert  m x_tVert^2-\lVert  m x_{t+1}Vert^2}{2\eta_t}+\sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\langle  m x_{t+1}- m x_t, m u_tangle}{\eta_t}+\sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\eta_t}{2} \lVert 
abla \ell_t(x_t)Vert^2 
onumber\ &\overset{(a)}{\le} rac{\lVert  m x_1Vert^2-\lVert  m x_{T+1}Vert^2}{2\eta_T}+ rac{\langle  m x_{T+1}, m u_Tangle}{\eta_T}- rac{\langle  m x_{1}, m u_1angle}{\eta_1}+\sum_{t=2}^T  rac{\langle  m u_{t-1}- m u_t, m x_tangle}{\eta_t}+\sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\eta_t}{2} \lVert 
abla \ell_t(x_t)Vert^2 
onumber\ &\le  rac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+ rac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\eta_t}{2} \lVert 
abla \ell_t(x_t)Vert^2, \end{align} where (a) uses the property that $\eta_1\ge \eta_2\ge \cdots \ge \eta_T$.
nodes.statement_short: Dynamic regret of projected gradient descent

nodes.name: Define the surrogate loss
nodes.statement: Moving back to the bandit-feedback model, following the proof of \citet[Theorem 8]{zhao2021bandit}, we can consider a loss function defined as $\widetilde \ell_t(x)\triangleq \ell_t(x)+\langle \bm x,\bm g_t-\nabla \ell_t(\bm x_t)\rangle$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the surrogate loss

nodes.name: Apply the full-feedback bound to the surrogate
nodes.statement:
As $
abla \widetilde \ell_t( m x_t)= m g_t$ and $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\widetilde \ell_t( m x)]=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\ell_t( m x)]$ (which is due to the fact that $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[ m g_t]=
abla \ell_t( m x_t)$), applying \Cref{eq:full information OGD D-Regret} gives  egin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t( m x_t)-\ell_t( m u_t))=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\widetilde \ell_t( m x_t)-\widetilde \ell_t( m u_t))ight ]\ &\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [ rac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+ rac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\eta_t}{2} \lVert 
abla \widetilde \ell_t( m x_t)Vert^2ight ]\overset{(b)}{\le}  rac{7R^2}{4\eta_T}+ rac{P_T R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T  rac{\eta_t}{2} C_t^2, \end{align*} where the expectation is taken 	extit{w.r.t.} the randomness in the stochastic gradient $\{ m g_t\}_{t\in [T]}$, and (b) makes use of the fact that $
abla \widetilde \ell_t( m x_t)= m g_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the full-feedback bound to the surrogate; conclude

nodes.name: Loss bound $C_t$ and Lipschitz constant $L_t$
nodes.statement: For loss function $\ell_t(\bm \lambda)=\langle \bm Q(t),\bm \lambda\rangle - Vg_t(\bm \lambda)$, it is bounded by $C_t\triangleq \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + V G$ and is $L_t\triangleq (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)$-Lipschitz. As $\bm Q(t)$ is revealed after the $(t-1)$-th round, $G_t$ and $L_t$ are both $\mathcal F_{t-1}$-measurable.
nodes.statement_short: Loss bound $C_t$ and Lipschitz constant $L_t$

nodes.name: Plan: tune $\delta_t$ for fixed $\eta_t$
nodes.statement: As sketched in the main text, we first regard $\eta_t$ as a constant and tune $\delta_t$ to minimize the summation term in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee}.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: tune $\delta_t$ for fixed $\eta_t$

nodes.name: Regret decomposition with tuned $\delta_t$
nodes.statement: Let $\delta_t=(\eta_t d^2 C_t^2 / L_t)^{1/3}$ and $\alpha_t=\delta_t / r$. Suppose that all conditions in \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee} hold, then \begin{align} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t)-\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t^\ast))\right ]\le \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{7R^2 + 4 P_T R}{4\eta_T} + \sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t \frac{d^2}{\delta_t^2} C_t^2 + 3L_t\delta_t + L_t \alpha_t R\right )\right ] \nonumber\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{\eta_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t d^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3} \frac{R}{r}\right ]\right ). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Regret decomposition with tuned $\delta_t$

nodes.name: Simplified learning rate
nodes.statement: We first only keep the last term in \Cref{eq:true learning rate in BCO appendix}, \textit{i.e.}, let \begin{equation} \eta_t = \left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\middle / \sum_{s=1}^t \left ((\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4}, \end{equation} then we have $\eta_1>\eta_2>\cdots >\eta_T$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplified learning rate

nodes.name: Apply the 3/4 summation lemma
nodes.statement: Let's first pretend the other condition of $\alpha_t<1$ from \Cref{lem:ABGD guarantee} also holds at this moment. \Cref{lem:3/4 summation lemma} reveals that if $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, then $\left .\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \middle / (\sum_{s\le t} x_s)^{1/4} \right . =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4}\right )$. Plugging in $x_t=\left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}$, \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t)-\ell_t(\bm \lambda_t^\ast))\right ] \\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} R \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4} \right ]\right . + \\ &\qquad \left .\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R}{r} \left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\right )^{1/4} d^{2/3} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4} \right ] \right )\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\right ), \end{align*} where the last step utilizes $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty \le \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the 3/4 summation lemma

nodes.name: It remains to ensure $\alpha_t<1$
nodes.statement: This almost recovers our conclusion, so it only remains to ensure $\alpha_t=\delta_t/r<1$, which is equivalent to $\eta_t d^2 C_t^2 / L_t < r^3$, \textit{i.e.}, \begin{equation*} \eta_t^{-1} > r^{-3} d^2 \frac{(\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2}{\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: It remains to ensure $\alpha_t<1$

nodes.name: Add a term $X$ to the denominator
nodes.statement: Consider adding a term $X$ into the denominator of \Cref{eq:learning rate in BCO}. As $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty \le \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2$, $(\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 / (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)\le 2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty^2 / \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2) + 2 ((VG)^2 / (VL))\le 2 \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + 2 VG^2 / L$. So we only need to show \begin{align*} \frac{\left (X + \sum_{s=1}^t \left ((\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4}}{(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{3/4}} > 2 r^{-3} d^2 \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + V \frac{G^2}{L}\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Add a term $X$ to the denominator

nodes.name: Split $X=X_1+X_2$
nodes.statement: We decompose $X$ into $X_1$ and $X_2$ and use them to cancel the two terms on the RHS, respectively. That is, we want \begin{align*} X_1 + \sum_{s=1}^t \left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty^2 \lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2^2\right )^{1/3} & > C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} \left (r^{-3} d^2 \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty\right )^{4/3},\\ X_2 + t^{3/4} (V^4 G^2 L^2)^{1/4} & > C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} \left (r^{-3} d^2 V G^2 / L\right )^{4/3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split $X=X_1+X_2$

nodes.name: Construct $X_1$ via the 4/3 lower bound and AM-GM
nodes.statement: We first craft $X_1$. In \Cref{lem:4/3 lower bound}, we show that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_t\rvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge (x_T/4)^{7/3}$. Thus, using the fact that $\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty\le \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2$ and the queue length increment bound $\lvert \lVert \bm Q(t+1)\rVert_\infty - \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty \rvert\le (2NM+R)$ (\Cref{lem:queue length increment}), we can let $x_t=\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty / (2NM+R)$ and lower bound the LHS by \begin{equation*} X_1 + \sum_{s=1}^t \left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_\infty^2 \lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2^2\right )^{1/3}\ge X_1+\frac{\left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty / 4 \right )^{7/3}}{(2NM+R)}\ge X_1^{3/7} \left (\frac{\left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty / 4 \right )^{7/3}}{(2NM+R)}\right )^{4/7}, \end{equation*} where the inequality results from AM-GM inequality $\frac{ax + by}{a+b} \ge \sqrt[a+b]{x^a y^b}$. Therefore, we only need to ensure $X_1^{3/7}\ge C^r T^{1/2-\delta_r} (4 r^{-3} d^2)^{4/3} (2NM+R)^{4/7}$. Setting $X_1$ as following then suffices. \begin{equation*} X_1=\left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}\right )^{7/3} \left (4r^{-3} d^2 \right )^{28/9} \left ((2NM+R)\right )^{4/3}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Construct $X_1$ via the 4/3 lower bound and AM-GM

nodes.name: Set $X_2$
nodes.statement: For $X_2$, we only need to set $X_2 = C^r T^{1/2-\delta_r} (r^{-3} d^2 VG^2 / L)^{4/3}$. Plugging back $X=X_1+X_2$, we get the learning rate scheduling defined in \Cref{eq:true learning rate in BCO appendix}.
nodes.statement_short: Set $X_2$; recover the learning rate

nodes.name: First regret term stays bounded
nodes.statement: Now we verify that the two terms on the RHS of \Cref{eq:BCO regret decomposition} does not increase too much due to $X$. For the first term, \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{\eta_T}\right ]\\ &=\left [\frac{R^2 + C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R}{(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{3/4}}\left (X + \sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r} R\right ) \left (\frac{X}{C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r}}\right )^{3/4}+(C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} R \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3} \right )^{3/4}\right ]\right )\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O} \left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^r T^{1/2-\delta_r})^2 + R (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{s=1}^t \left (\lVert \bm q_s\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3} \right )^{3/4}\right ]\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: First regret term stays bounded

nodes.name: Second term via the summation lemma
nodes.statement: For the second term, as $\eta_t$ is strictly smaller than that in \Cref{eq:learning rate in BCO}, we can again apply \Cref{lem:3/4 summation lemma} (if $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T\ge 0$, then $\left .\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \middle / (\sum_{s\le t} x_s)^{1/4} \right . =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4}\right )$) to conclude \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\eta_t d^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_\infty + VG)^2 (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + VL)^2\right )^{1/3} \frac{R}{r}\right ]\\ &=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3} (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Second term via the summation lemma

nodes.name: Sum both parts
nodes.statement: Summing up two parts gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Sum both parts

nodes.name: Self-bounding inequality from the calculation lemma
nodes.statement: As sketched in the main text, the first step is to \textit{i)} combine algorithmic guarantees for \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace (\Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making}) and \texttt{AdaBGD}\xspace (\Cref{thm:multi-hop utility decision making}), \textit{ii)} plug in the network stability assumption \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility network stability}, and \textit{iii)} make use of the Lyapunov DPP analysis in \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility Lyapunov}. Deferring these calculations to \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility tedious calc}, we can get \begin{align} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ] + f(T) + \nonumber \\ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] + \nonumber \\ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{7/8}. \end{align} where \begin{align*} f(T)&= \epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T + \frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2\right .+\\ &\qquad \qquad \left .\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+\frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T\right ),\\ g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4} M \sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2 - \delta_a}} \log T \right ), \\ h(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/8} \left (\frac Rr d^{2/3} + R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4}\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Self-bounding inequality from the calculation lemma
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Step 1: coarse queue bound
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 1 (Develop a Coarse Average Queue Length Bound).} Recall the assumption that $g_t$ is uniformly bounded by $[-G,G]$. Therefore, the first term on the RHS of \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding} is bounded by $2\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT$ in absolute value. In \Cref{lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding}, we develop a self-bounding property that says, if $y\le f+y^{3/4} g \log y +y^{7/8}$, then $y=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (f+g^4 \log^8\left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right )+h^8\right )$. Therefore, applying it to \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding}, we have \begin{align} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (2\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T) + g(T)^4 \log^8\left (2(f(T)^{1/8}+g(T)^{1/2}+h(T))^2\right ) + h(T)^8\right ) \nonumber\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)\right ) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T\left (T^{1-2\delta_a} \log^8 \left (T^{1/4} + T^{1/4-\delta_a/2} + T^{1/4-\delta_\lambda/2}\right ) + T^{1-2\delta_\lambda}\right ) \nonumber\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)\right )+o_T(1). \end{align} As mentioned in the proof sketch of this theorem, this only gives a $\frac 1T\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1]=\operatorname{\mathcal O}_T(V)$ bound on the average queue length, which violates the system stability condition \Cref{eq:average queue}. However, this inequality can be used to derive the polynomial convergence result on the utility, which in turn refines the average queue length bound.
nodes.statement_short: Step 1: coarse queue bound
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Step 2: utility gap $O(1/V)$
nodes.statement:
\paragraph{Step 2 (Yield Polynomial Convergence on the Utility).} Moving the difference in the average utility in \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding} to the LHS, we have  egin{align*}  rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ]&\le -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ] + f(T) + 
onumber \ &\quad g(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ] + 
onumber \ &\quad h(T) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert  m Q(t)Vert_1ight ]^{7/8}. \end{align*} Plugging in the just-derived bound on average queue length, namely \Cref{eq:coarse queue length bound}, we have  egin{align*} &\quad  rac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T  igg (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)) igg )ight ]\ &\le 0 + f(T) + g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight )^{3/4} \log \left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight ) + h(T) \left ( rac{V}{\epsilon_W} GT + f(T)ight )^{7/8}ight )\ &=f(T) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}_T \left (T^{1/4 - \delta_a/2} (VT)^{3/4} \log(VT) + T^{1/8 - \delta_\lambda / 4} (VT)^{7/8}ight ). \end{align*} According to the assumption that $V=o_T(\min\{T^{2\delta_a/3},T^{2\delta_\lambda/7}\})$, the second term on the RHS is of order $o_T(T)$. Therefore, we have  egin{align} &\quad  rac 1T \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left (g_t(\mathring{ m \lambda}(t)) - g_t( m \lambda(t)))ight )ight ]= rac{\epsilon_W}{VT} f(T) +  rac{\epsilon_W}{VT} o_T(T) 
onumber \ &=(VT)^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T +  rac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2ight .+ 
onumber\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad \left .\left ( rac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+Right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+ rac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) Tight )+o_T(V^{-1}) 
onumber\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ( rac{(N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W + (N^4 M^2+N^2 R^2)}{V}ight ) + o_T(V^{-1}). \end{align} The second conclusion of this theorem follows.
nodes.statement_short: Step 2: utility gap $O(1/V)$
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Step 3: refined queue bound
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Step 3 (Refine the Average Queue Length Bound).} Now we are ready to refine our average queue length bound using \Cref{eq:refined utility bound}. Instead of controlling the utility with the uniform boundedness assumption that $g_t\in [-G,G]$, we utilize the just-derived convergence result \Cref{eq:refined utility bound}. Specifically, again applying the self-bounding property in \Cref{lem:3/4 and 7/8 self-bounding} to \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility self-bounding} but instead replacing the first term on the RHS with \Cref{eq:refined utility bound}, we get \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (f(T) + o_T(T) + f(T) + g(T)^4 \log^8\left (2(f(T)^{1/8}+g(T)^{1/2}+h(T))^2\right ) + h(T)^8\right )\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}(f(T)) + \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (g(T)^4 \log^8\left (2(f(T)^{1/8}+g(T)^{1/2}+h(T))^2\right ) + h(T)^8\right ) + o_T(T) \\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\frac{(N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W + (N^4 M^2+N^2 R^2)}{\epsilon_W} T\right ) + o_T(T), \end{align*} which gives our first conclusion as well.
nodes.statement_short: Step 3: refined queue bound
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Reference-policy stability bound
nodes.statement: From the network stability assumption, we derived in \Cref{lem:multi-hop utility network stability} that \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \nonumber\\ &\le -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mathring \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))\right ] - \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \mathring \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reference-policy stability bound
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Recall the AdaPFOL and AdaBGD guarantees and combine
nodes.statement: Recall the \texttt{AdaPFOL}\xspace guarantee in \Cref{thm:multi-hop stability decision making} that \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} (\mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t)-\mathring{\mu}_{n,m}^{(k)}(t))\left (Q_m^{(k)}(t)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right )\right ]\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M\sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right )\text{,} \end{align*} and the Bandit Convex Optimization guarantee in \Cref{thm:multi-hop utility decision making} that \begin{align*} &\scalemath{0.95}{\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \left ((\langle \bm Q(t),\bm \lambda(t)\rangle - Vg_t(\bm \lambda(t))) - (\langle \bm Q(t),\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)\rangle - Vg_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right )\right ]}\\ &\scalemath{0.95}{=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^2\right )+\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\right ),} \end{align*} we therefore have \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \nonumber\\ &\le -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}}\sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \mu_{n,m}^{(k)}(t) (Q_m^{(k)}(t) - Q_n^{(k)}(t))\right ] + \\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right )+\\ &\quad - \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t) \lambda_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t))-g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ]+\\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^2\right )+\\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the AdaPFOL and AdaBGD guarantees and combine
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Plug in the DPP inequality
nodes.statement: Further plugging in the Lyapunov DPP calculation in \Cref{eq:multi-hop utility Lyapunov} (which controls the three $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[\sum_{t=1}^T \cdots]$ terms outside $\operatorname{\mathcal O}$ on the RHS), we have \begin{align*} &\quad \epsilon_W \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)\right ] - (N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T \nonumber\\ &\le \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M \sqrt{1+P_T^a} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2} \log T \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\right ]\right )+\\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2-\delta_\lambda})^2\right )+\\ &\quad \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2 + V(L+G)\right )^{4/3}\right )^{3/4}\right ]\right )+\\ &\quad \frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2)+V \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T (g_t(\bm \lambda(t))-g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)))\right ]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Plug in the DPP inequality
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Abbreviate with $\widetilde f,\widetilde g,\widetilde h$
nodes.statement: For notational simplicity, we can abbreviate this inequality as \begin{align*} &\quad \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ]+\widetilde f(T)+\\ &\quad \widetilde g(T) \sqrt{\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2\right ]} \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t)-\bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right ) + \widetilde h(T) \left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^{4/3}\right ]\right )^{3/4}, \end{align*} where \begin{align*} \widetilde f(T)&= \epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((N^2 (2NM+R)^2 + \epsilon_W N^2 (2NM+R)) C_W T + \frac{R(2NM+R)}{r^7} d^{14/3} (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^2\right .+\\ &\qquad \qquad \left .\left (\frac{R}{r} d^{2/3}+R\right ) (C^r T^{1/2 - \delta_r})^{1/4} V(L+G) T^{3/4}+\frac 12 N^2 ((NM)^2+2(NM)^2+2R^2) T\right ),\\ \widetilde g(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (M \sqrt{1+C^a T^{1/2 - \delta_a}} \log T \right ), \\ \widetilde h(T)&=\epsilon_W^{-1} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (\frac Rr d^{2/3} + R\right ) (C^\lambda T^{1/2 - \delta_\lambda})^{1/4}\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Abbreviate with $\widetilde f,\widetilde g,\widetilde h$
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Bound squared queue sums
nodes.statement: To handle the $\widetilde g(T)$-related term, we use the argument same to that of \Cref{sec:multi-hop stability main theorem}: \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} states that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_t\rvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^2 = \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{3/2}\right )$. From \Cref{lem:queue length increment}, any single queue $Q_n^{(k)}(t)$ satisfies $\lvert Q_n^{(k)}(t+1)-Q_n^{(k)}(t)\rvert \le (2NM + R)$. Hence, applying \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} to $\{Q_n^{(k)}(t) / (2NM+R)\}_{t\in [T]}$ to every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2 = (2NM+R)^2 \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} \left (\frac{Q_n^{(k)}(t)}{2NM+R}\right )^2 =\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\sqrt{2NM+R} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{1.5}\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound squared queue sums
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Bound the $\widetilde g$ term
nodes.statement: Further noticing that \begin{equation*} \max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t) - \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\le \sum_{t=1}^T M \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \lVert \bm Q_n(t)\rVert_1\le M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1, \end{equation*} the $\widetilde g(T)$-related term then becomes \begin{align*} &\quad \widetilde g(T) \sqrt{\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^2\right ]} \log \left (\max_{t=1}^T \max_{(n,m)\in {\mathcal L}} M \lVert \bm Q_m(t)-\bm Q_n(t)\rVert_\infty\right )\\ &=\widetilde g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{3/4} \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )\right ]\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $\widetilde g$ term
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Jensen's inequality
nodes.statement: Noticing that $x\mapsto x^{3/4} \log (M x)$ is concave when $x$ is large enough, Jensen inequality then gives \begin{equation*} \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{3/4} \log \left (M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ) \right ]\right )= \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}} \left [ \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Bound the $\widetilde h$ term via the 4/3 upper bound
nodes.statement: Moreover, we handle the $\widetilde h(T)$-related term using \Cref{lem:4/3 upper bound}, a variant of \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} which states that if $x_1=0$, $x_2,\ldots,x_T \ge 0$, and $\lvert x_{t+1}-x_t\rvert\le 1$, then $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} = \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((\sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{7/6}\right )$. Hence, still applying it to $\{Q_n^{(k)}(t) / (2NM + R)\}_{t\in [T]}$ for every $n\in {\mathcal N}$ and $k\in {\mathcal N}$, \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_2^{4/3}&=\sum_{t=1}^T \left (\sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)^2\right )^{2/3}\le \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{n\in {\mathcal N}} \sum_{k\in {\mathcal N}} Q_n^{(k)}(t)^{4/3}\\ &=\operatorname{\mathcal O}\left (\left (2NM+R\right )^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right )^{7/6}\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $\widetilde h$ term via the 4/3 upper bound
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Therefore, we have \begin{align*} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]&\le -\frac{V}{\epsilon_W} \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \bigg (g_t(\mathring{\bm \lambda}(t)) - g_t(\bm \lambda(t))\bigg )\right ] + \widetilde f(T) + \\ &\quad \widetilde g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/4}\right ) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{3/4} \log \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [M \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ] + \\ &\quad \widetilde h(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}\left ((2NM+R)^{1/8}\right ) \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\left [\sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \bm Q(t)\rVert_1\right ]^{7/8}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Define $f,g,h$
nodes.statement: Setting $f(T)=\widetilde f(T)$, $g(T)=\widetilde g(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}((2NM+R)^{1/4})$, and $h(T)=\widetilde h(T) \operatorname{\mathcal O}((2NM+R)^{1/8})$ gives our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Define $f,g,h$; conclude
nodes.section: C.5 Main Theorem for Multi-Hop Utility Maximization (Proof of 4.5)

nodes.name: Induction on $T$
nodes.statement: Prove by induction. The case when $T=1$ is obvious.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $T$; base case

nodes.name: Inductive step: reduce to a one-term inequality
nodes.statement: Suppose that the conclusion holds for $T-1$, then consider some $x_T$: \begin{align*} &\quad \sum_{t=1}^T \frac{x_t}{\left (\sum_{s=1}^t x_s\right )^{1/4}}\\ &= \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \frac{x_t}{\left (\sum_{s=1}^t x_s\right )^{1/4}} + \frac{x_T}{\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}}\\ &\le 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{3/4} + \frac{x_T}{\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}}, \end{align*} so it suffices to prove $\left . x_T \middle / \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}\right .\le 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4} - 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{3/4}$.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step: reduce to a one-term inequality

nodes.name: Elementary inequality between partial sums
nodes.statement: Notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{3/4} - \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{3/4}\right )\left (\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}+\left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{1/4}\right )\\ &=\left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \right ) + \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \right )^{3/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t \right )^{1/4} - \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t \right )^{1/4} \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t \right )^{3/4} - \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t \right ) \\ &\ge x_T, \end{align*} where the last inequality uses $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\ge \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t$ (follows from $x_T\ge 0$).
nodes.statement_short: Elementary inequality between partial sums

nodes.name: Close the induction
nodes.statement: Hence, due to the fact that \begin{equation*} \left . x_T \middle / 2 \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4}\right .\le \left . x_T \middle / \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/4} + \left (\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} x_t\right )^{1/4}\right ., \end{equation*} the conclusion holds for $T$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: Close the induction

nodes.name: Last terms stay large
nodes.statement: As adjacent $x_t$'s differ by no more than $1$, $\lfloor x_T\rfloor < T$ and $x_{T-t}\ge x_T - t$.
nodes.statement_short: Last terms stay large

nodes.name: Lower-bound by a power sum
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} x_{T-t}^{4/3}\ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} (x_T-t)^{4/3} \ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} \left (t^{4/3} + (x_T - \lfloor x_T\rfloor)^{4/3}\right )\ge \sum_{t=0}^{\lfloor x_T\rfloor} t^{4/3}, \end{equation*} where the last step uses $(a+b)^{4/3} \ge a^{4/3} + b^{4/3}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound by a power sum

nodes.name: Estimate the power sum
nodes.statement: As \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=0}^n i^{4/3} \ge \sum_{i=\lfloor \frac n2 \rfloor}^n i^{4/3} \ge \left (n - \left \lfloor \frac n2 \right \rfloor\right ) \left (\left \lfloor \frac n2 \right \rfloor\right )^{4/3} \ge \left (\left \lfloor \frac n2 \right \rfloor\right )^{7/3}, \end{equation*} we have $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge (\lfloor \frac{x_T}{2}\rfloor )^{7/3}$.
nodes.statement_short: Estimate the power sum

nodes.name: Case $x_T\ge 4$
nodes.statement: If $x_T\ge 4$, then $\lfloor \frac{x_T}{2}\rfloor \ge \frac{x_T}{2}-1 \ge \frac{x_T}{4}$, giving the conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Case $x_T\ge 4$

nodes.name: Case $x_T<4$
nodes.statement: Otherwise, \textit{i.e.}, $x_T<4$, then we naturally have $\sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \ge (\frac{x_T}{4})^{4/3}\ge (\frac{x_T}{4})^{7/3}$, so our conclusion still follows.
nodes.statement_short: Case $x_T<4$

nodes.name: Sort the sequence as in Huang et al.
nodes.statement: Imitating the proof of \Cref{lem:2 upper bound} \citep[Lemma 4]{huang2023queue}, we short $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_T$ as $y_1\le y_2\le \cdots \le y_T$.
nodes.statement_short: Sort the sequence as in Huang et al.

nodes.name: Maximum bounded by $(2\sum x_t)^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: According to the original proof, $y_T=\max_{t\in [T]} x_t\le (2 \sum_{t=1}^T x_t)^{1/2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximum bounded by $(2\sum x_t)^{1/2}$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t^{4/3} \le y_T^{1/3} \sum_{t=1}^T x_t \le \left (2 \sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right ) = 2^{1/6} \left (\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\right )^{7/6}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Conclude

nodes.name: Define $i(z)$ and expand the candidate bound
nodes.statement: Let $i(z) = z^4 - z^3 g \log (z^4) - f$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )^4\\ &\ge f + 4 \left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )^3 g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $i(z)$ and expand the candidate bound

nodes.name: $i$ is nonnegative at the candidate
nodes.statement: As $f,g\ge 1$, we have $2 (f^{1/4} + g)^2\ge f^{1/4} + g \log (2 (f^{1/4} + g)^2)$. Applying this relationship to the second log on the RHS of the inequality above, we yield \begin{equation*} i\left (f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\right )\ge 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $i$ is nonnegative at the candidate

nodes.name: Reduce to monotonicity of $i$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from the conditions, we know $i(y^{1/4})\le 0$. Hence, if we can prove that $i(z)$ is monotone (at least for a range of $z$), we can conclude that $y^{1/4}\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )$, thus giving our conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to monotonicity of $i$

nodes.name: Compute $i'(z)$
nodes.statement: To conclude the monotonity of $i(z)$, we calculate its derivative as \begin{equation*} i'(z) = 4z^3 - 3z^2 g \log (z^4) - 4z^2 g. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute $i'(z)$

nodes.name: $i$ increasing beyond $z_0$
nodes.statement: Thus, if we only consider the case where $z\ge 0$, $i'(z)\ge 0$ holds when $z\ge 3g\log z + g$. Denoting the larger root of $z=3g\log z+g$ as $z_0$ (in case it has no root, let $z_0=1$), we know $i(z)$ is increasing in $[z_0,+\infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: $i$ increasing beyond $z_0$

nodes.name: Candidate exceeds $z_0$
nodes.statement: Further observing that $f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )$ indeed satisfies $z\ge 3g\log z + g$, we know $f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right )\ge z_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Candidate exceeds $z_0$

nodes.name: Compare $y^{1/4}$ with $z_0$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from the assumption that $y\le f + y^{3/4} g \log y$, we know $i(y^{1/4})\le 0\le i(f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ))$. Our conclusion follows from discussing the relationship between $y^{1/4}$ and $z_0$:
nodes.statement_short: Compare $y^{1/4}$ with $z_0$

nodes.name: Case $y^{1/4}\le z_0$
nodes.statement: If $y^{1/4}\le z_0$, then we immediately have \begin{equation*} y^{1/4}\le z_0\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Case $y^{1/4}\le z_0$

nodes.name: Case $y^{1/4}>z_0$
nodes.statement: Otherwise, according to the monotonity of $i(z)$ when $z\ge z_0$, we still have \begin{equation*} y^{1/4}\le f^{1/4} + g \log \left (2(f^{1/4} + g)^2\right ), \end{equation*} as claimed.

nodes.name: Define $i(z)$ and expand the candidate bound
nodes.statement: Let $i(z) = z^8 - f - z^6 g \log (z^8) - z^7 h$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^8 \\ &=\left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right )\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 h\\ &\ge \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^6 f^{1/4} + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^6 g \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 h \\ &\ge f + \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^6 g \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + \\ &\quad \left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h\right )^7 h. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $i(z)$ and expand the candidate bound

nodes.name: $i$ is nonnegative at the candidate
nodes.statement: As $f,g,h\ge 1$, we have $2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\ge f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h$. Applying it to the $(\cdots)^6 g \log(2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2)$ term on the RHS, we have \begin{equation*} i\left (f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right )+h\right )\ge 0 \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $i$ is nonnegative at the candidate

nodes.name: Reduce to monotonicity of $i$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from the conditions we know $i(y^{1/8})\le 0$. Hence, we again want to prove the monotony of $i(z)$, which gives the conclusion that $y^{1/8}\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} + h$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to monotonicity of $i$

nodes.name: Compute $i'(z)$
nodes.statement: Calculating the derivative of $i(z)$, we have \begin{equation*} i'(z) = 8z^7 - 6z^5 g \log(z^8) - 8 z^5 g - 7z^6 h. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute $i'(z)$

nodes.name: $i$ monotone beyond $z_0$
nodes.statement: Thus, if we only consider the case where $z\ge 1$, $i'(z)\ge 0$ holds when $8z^2 - 6 g \log(z^8) - 8 g - 7z h\ge 0$. As $z^2$ is convex and $6g\log (z^8) + 8g + 7zh$ is concave, there are at most two intersections. Hence, again denoting the larger root of $8z^2 - 6 g \log(z^8) - 8 g - 7z h = 0$ as $z_0$ (in case there is no root, let $z_0=1$), $i(z)$ is monotonic in $[z_0,+\infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: $i$ monotone beyond $z_0$

nodes.name: Candidate exceeds $z_0$
nodes.statement: As $f,g,h\ge 1$, $f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h \ge z_0$ always holds. The conclusion follows by discussing the relationship of $y^{1/8}$ and $z_0$:
nodes.statement_short: Candidate exceeds $z_0$; compare $y^{1/8}$ with $z_0$

nodes.name: Case $y^{1/8}\le z_0$
nodes.statement: If $y^{1/8}\le z_0$, we directly have \begin{equation*} y^{1/8}\le z_0\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Case $y^{1/8}\le z_0$

nodes.name: Case $y^{1/8}>z_0$
nodes.statement: Otherwise, we can still conclude \begin{equation*} y^{1/8}\le f^{1/8} + g^{1/2} \log \left (2(f^{1/8}+g^{1/2}+h)^2\right ) + h \end{equation*} from the monotonity of $i(z)$ when $z\ge z_0$.

Calculate this round's action $\bm x_t\in \mathcal X$, observe loss $\ell_t(x_t)$, and update internal variable $\bm y_{t+1}$:
\begin{equation} \bm x_t=\bm y_t+\delta \bm s_t,\quad \bm y_{t+1}=\text{Proj}_{(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal X}\left [\bm y_t-\eta_t \frac{d}{\delta_t} \ell_t(\bm x_t) \bm s_t\right ],
\end{equation}
where $\bm s_t\in \mathbb R^d$ is a uniformly sampled unit vector used to estimate gradients \citep{flaxman2005online}.
